newsitem.title: HONG KONG: United freighter conversion for Asia starts.
newsitem.headline: United freighter conversion for Asia starts.

text.p: Work is under way to convert the first two aircraft for United Airlines' new all-cargo service to Asia, senior vice-president international, Chris Bowers said.
Speaking in a telephone interview from United's headquarters in Chicago, Bowers told Reuters the service, originally due to have started this autumn, is now on schedule to begin next March.

The service was due to link Tokyo, Osaka, Taipei and Manila with New York, Chicago, Los Angeles and San Francisco but United said in August it could not get the aircraft it wanted in time, causing a delay.
Bowers said freighter conversion work on the first two of four former passenger DC-10-30 airliners is in progress.
"Cargo has been and will continue to be an important product for us. We have not had a dedicated cargo fleet for 10 or 15 years so we're going back into that," he added.
United's entry into the expanding Asian cargo market is being seen as a significant revenue earning attempt away from its north American base.
"We are pleased with the cargo business that we have in the bellies of our airplanes and still believe there's potential on the upside in Asia Pacific," he said.
United will be able to utilise its wide-ranging U.S. domestic and international route network and benefit from its alliance with Deutsche Lufthansa AG, he added.

"We think we are at a competitive advantage because of our route network. We know it's going to be very competitive but are happy to compete and think we will do just fine," he said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
